texts.value: Component of the nuclear lamina, a fibrous layer on the nucleoplasmic side of the inner nuclear membrane, which is thought to provide a framework for the nuclear envelope and interacts with chromatin (PubMed:10077600, PubMed:15035436, PubMed:22393432, PubMed:3126192, PubMed:9394018). Essential for nuclear envelope assembly; required for the association of membrane vesicle nuclear envelope precursors with decondensing chromatin (PubMed:1527167). Involved in the organization and spacing of nuclear pore complexes on the nucleus surface; complements LamC (PubMed:15996653). May have a role in the localization of the LEM domain proteins Ote, bocks and MAN1 to the nuclear membrane (PubMed:15035436, PubMed:16439308). Required for uniform distribution of type-A lamin LamC within the nuclear lamina (PubMed:15996653). In spermatocytes, plays a role in maintaining LamC nuclear localization; regulates meiotic cytokinesis by maintaining the structure of the spindle envelope, and by contributing to the formation of the contractile ring and central spindle (PubMed:27402967). Required for nuclear migration and to link the microtubule organizing center (MTOC) to the nucleus (PubMed:14617811). In addition, is required for nuclear envelope localization of klar (PubMed:14617811). Maternal expression is critical for embryogenesis (PubMed:15054108). Involved in dorsal-ventral patterning in oocytes (PubMed:11533666). Required for structural organization of cytoplasmic processes during tracheal terminal branch outgrowth (PubMed:11533666). Zygotic expression is critical for late larval and pupal development (PubMed:15996653). May be involved in the nuclear localization or stability of the ecdysone receptor EcR (PubMed:15996653)

Homodimerizes via a coiled-coil interaction of the intermediate filament (IF) rod domain; dimerization does not depend on the phosphorylation state of Ser-25 (PubMed:8537453, PubMed:8776884). Homodimers form higher order oligomers and polymers via multiple interactions, including longitudinal head-to-tail interactions and lateral interactions (PubMed:8776884). Head-to-tail oligomers form by interactions between the N-terminal coil 1A region of the IF rod domain of one homodimer and the C-terminal coil 2 region of the IF rod domain of another homodimer (PubMed:8776884). Head-to-tail oligomerization is regulated by phosphorylation (PubMed:9013881). Interacts with LBR; the interaction is direct (PubMed:15054108). Interacts with MAN1 (PubMed:16439308). Interacts with Ote (PubMed:22751930, PubMed:9632815). Associates (via C-terminus) with chromatin probably through an interaction with H2A or H2B; interaction is more efficient when polymerized (PubMed:10077600, PubMed:1527167, PubMed:22393432, PubMed:8603728, PubMed:9394018)

At metaphase and anaphase, weakly expressed in the nuclear envelope and spindle poles (PubMed:16439308). Expression in oocyte cytoplasm increases after stages 6 to 7 of egg development (PubMed:9199347). In spermatocytes detected at the spindle envelope, spindle poles and astral membrane throughout meiosis I, whereas mostly depleted in meiosis II (PubMed:27402967). Colocalizes with nuclear pore complex component Nup107 throughout meiosis I (PubMed:27402967). Cytoplasmic lamin is more soluble than nuclear lamin (PubMed:2492999). Oocytes also possess an intranuclear pool not associated with the lamina (PubMed:2492999). A cytoplasmic pool is detectable surrounding the oocyte nucleus and nuclei of embryos during the first 3 hours of embryogenesis (PubMed:21989239, PubMed:2492999)

Constitutively expressed in all tissues and cells (at protein level) (PubMed:7593280, PubMed:8537453). Expressed in spermatocytes but not in mature sperm (at protein level) (PubMed:27402967). Expressed in the nuclei of nurse cells, follicle cells and oocyte during oogenesis (PubMed:2492999)

Expressed both maternally and zygotically during embryogenesis (at protein level) (PubMed:15996653, PubMed:21989239). Constitutively expressed in all stages of embryogenesis, especially during the first 6-9 hours (at protein level) (PubMed:21989239, PubMed:7593280)

Three forms of lamin have been identified in D.melanogaster, lamin Dm0 is rapidly processed to lamin Dm1 in the cytoplasm, Dm1 is then assembled in the nuclear envelope and is phosphorylated, forming lamin Dm2 (PubMed:18327897, PubMed:3126192, PubMed:8537453). Cells undergoing mitosis or meiosis, or trapped in mitosis by drugs, possess an alternatively phosphorylated form called Dm(mit); this form is more soluble, correlating with nuclear disassembly (PubMed:2492999)

Phosphorylation by CDK1 on Ser-42 and Ser-45 or by PKA on Ser-50 interferes with head-to-tail oligomerization and stimulates lamin disassembly (PubMed:9013881). During interphase can be phosphorylated on Ser-25, Thr-435 and Ser-595 (PubMed:10194384, PubMed:12378269). During mitosis the soluble form known as Dm(mit) is phosphorylated on Ser-45; a subset of molecules may also be phosphorylated on Ser-25 (PubMed:10194384)

Late pupal lethal (PubMed:15996653). After puparium formation development is delayed and ceases at the pharate adult stage (PubMed:15996653). Abnormal organogenesis at later stages of development, including retarded growth of gonad and central nervous system (PubMed:15996653). Ventriculus hypertrophy with increased cell proliferation but normal tissue organization (PubMed:15996653). Defective eye development with photoreceptor nuclei that fail to migrate apically as they are specified, resulting in aberrantly shaped photoreceptors in adult eyes (PubMed:14617811, PubMed:15996653). Some early knockout alleles result in embryonic lethality with terminal branches of the tracheal system following abnormal projection patterns during branch outgrowth (PubMed:11533666). RNAi-mediated knockdown in embryos arrests development at stage 10 of embryogenesis; cell nuclei are easily damaged and nuclear pore complexes form aggregates (PubMed:15054108). RNAi-mediated knockdown in spermatocytes results in spindle envelope disintegration, failure to form contractile rings and central spindle microtubules during meiosis I resulting in abnormal cytokinesis and multinuclear cell formation (PubMed:27402967)
Named 'misguided' due to the abnormal projection patterns of terminal branches during tracheal system development observed in mutant flies
Belongs to the intermediate filament family
